title: Winspace T1600 Review: An Aero Rocket 🚀 with Question Marks!

takeaways.text: Frame, cockpit and wheels supplied by Winspace. Build faults: a seatpost-clamp screw with no usable head (Winspace sent a replacement and promised better QC), an internal joint step that snagged the Di2 wire in the chainstay, and a computer mount drilled only for Garmin (since fixed in newer batches).
T47 bottom bracket and headset fitted without play; a built-in Di2 battery holder and a hidden front-derailleur wire port under the hanger; no printed manual.
His size-L Ultegra Di2 build with heavy LUN Mega D47 wheels, 28 mm tires, power-meter pedals, cages and mount weighed about 7.8 kg.

After 1,000+ km: very laterally stiff, especially out of the saddle, but firm rather than harsh (comfort 4/5 against his Agile's 5/5); comes alive above 35–40 km/h and was the most stable bike he had ridden in crosswinds.

Frameset US$2,400 in November 2025; complete bikes about US$6,300 with Dura-Ace Di2 or about US$5,300 with Ultegra before his discount code. Winspace said no import fees apply; he has not paid any in the EU on free-shipping orders.

disclosure: The creator says Winspace supplied the frame, wheels and handlebars, and discloses affiliate commissions and a Winspace discount code.
summary: T1600 build and ride review with equipment and issue discussion. The supplied review build does not select the catalog candidate's unresolved trim or establish T1600 Ultra specifications.
